title: Tautological quotient data and quotient-preserving classification on a projective bundle
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $E$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $A_S(E)$ be its canonical symmetric graded algebra [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra], and let $p:P=\operatorname{Proj}_S A_S(E)\to S$ be the relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj]. A tautological quotient datum consists of an invertible module $D.L$ on $P$ [def-sc-invertible-module], a surjection $D.q:p^*E\to D.L$ (using the module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]), and, on each affine open $U\subseteq S$, an isomorphism from the restriction of $D.L$ to the degree-one Proj twist $\mathcal O(1)$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. The chart isomorphism sends the pullback of each local section $e\in E(U)$ through $D.q$ to the degree-one homogeneous section $\iota(e)/1$ of that twist. For any scheme $T$, morphisms $h:T\to S$ and $a:T\to P$, and equality $h_a:p\circ a=h$, define the pulled quotient $h^*E\to a^*D.L$ by the canonical identification $h^*E\simeq a^*p^*E$ followed by $a^*D.q$. Given a module $L$ on $T$ and a map $q:h^*E\to L$, say that $a$ classifies $(L,q)$ relative to $D$ if there exist $h_a:p\circ a=h$ and an isomorphism $v:a^*D.L\simeq L$ such that the pulled quotient followed by $v$ equals $q$. This defines the datum, the pulled map and the classification relation; it asserts neither existence of a datum nor the projective-bundle universal property.
